name: Area Chart
hint: Drag across the overview strip: the plot springs to that window. Double-click resets.
description: Stacked or overlapping area chart for one measure split into a few parts over many points: your rows, your series, your formats. Its signature is brush to zoom: drag across the slim overview (or its handles, or the window itself) and the main plot's x-scale springs to that window, paths staying continuous while ticks re-flow and fade and the y-axis re-fits. A crosshair snaps to the nearest point with one glass tooltip listing every series plus the total, and arrow keys walk it. The legend toggles series and the stack re-settles on springs without repainting colours; flags on the x-axis open notes about events. Dates get a time axis whose ticks re-flow from quarters to days; anything else gets a category axis. The sample content (`demo`) is a year of household energy by source.
intents: stacked area chart with brush zoom
energy usage by source over a year
time series chart with zoomable overview
traffic by channel area chart with annotations
daily metrics chart with range selector
usage: Use for one measure split into 1 to 8 parts over many points, where the reader needs both the whole range and a close look at a stretch of it. Pass `data` (rows of plain objects), `xKey` (Date values give a time axis, strings or numbers a category axis) and `series: [{ key, label, tone }]` (or `yKey` for a single series); format numbers with `formatValue` / `formatAxis` and x labels with `formatX`. Own the zoom with `range` + `onRangeChange` ([start, end] row indices), the visible series with `hiddenSeries` + `onHiddenSeriesChange`, and the data states with `loading`, `error` + `onRetry` and `emptyMessage`. `onPointClick(row, index)` fires on click or Enter at the crosshair. Stack when the parts add up to a meaningful total; switch to overlap to compare shapes. One y-axis and one unit; values are drawn from 0 up (negatives are not plotted), and points are evenly spaced, one per row. The view switch (Chart / Table) and the Stacked / Overlap switch are the kit's shared `Segmented` control from components/_shared/chart.jsx, which has no slug of its own.

dataProps.description: Rows of plain objects, one per point, in x order. Each row holds the x value under `xKey` and one number per series under its key. Missing or non-numeric values draw as 0.
Field holding each row's x value. Date objects give a time axis; strings or numbers a category axis.
Shortcut for one series: the field holding its value (label = the key). Ignored when `series` is given.

[{ key, label, tone }]: which fields to draw, bottom of the stack first. `tone` is a series slot 0–7 or a --ts-* token name ("--ts-series-4"); default is the slot by position. Up to 8; lines after the first are dashed so series differ by more than hue.
[{ x | index, endX | endIndex, title, note }]: flags under the x axis with a note on hover, focus or tap. `x` is matched against the rows' x values (Dates by time).
Card title (also the chart's accessible name when a string).
Line under the title.
Hero slot above the plot: a node, or ({ rows, from, to, fromIndex, toIndex }) => node for figures that follow the zoom window.
(value, series) => string for tooltip, table and summary values. Default: Intl number in the Theme's locale, no unit.
(value) => string for y-axis ticks. Default: compact Intl number.
(x, { kind, sub, index }) => string for x labels; kind is "month", "tick" or "full" (tooltip, table). Default: Intl dates in the Theme's locale, other values as given.
Header of the x column in the table view.
Label of the stacked total in the tooltip and table.
Accessible name of the legend.
Text of the button that shows the whole range after zooming.
Controlled zoom window as [start, end] row indices. Pass with onRangeChange.
Uncontrolled starting window. Default: every row.
([start, end]) => void while the brush, its handles, the arrow keys, double-click or the reset button move the window.
Controlled list of series keys switched off in the legend. Pass with onHiddenSeriesChange.
Uncontrolled starting list of hidden series keys.
(keys) => void when a legend item is toggled.
("stacked" | "overlap") => void when the in-card switch is used. `mode` sets it from outside.
(row, index, event) => void on click, or Enter / Space with the plot focused, at the crosshair's point.
One-line text alternative read by screen readers. Default: series, point count, range and the highest value, from your formatters.
You are fetching: the plot shimmers (a placeholder area when there is no data yet) and is aria-busy.
Text of the busy chip while loading.
Shown in the plot box instead of the chart, with a retry button when onRetry is given.
() => void from the error form's Try again button.
Shown in the plot box when there are no rows.
Dash the lines of series after the first (and their legend keys). Default on; off in the sample.
The whole card inert: not focusable, dimmed, aria-disabled.
Accessible name when there is no string title (the aria-label attribute works too).
The card's <section> element.
Show the sample year of household energy (titles, kWh formats, events, the self-powered headline). Your own props win over it.

example:
<AreaChart
  data={weeks}            // [{ weekOf: Date, free: 120, pro: 40 }, …]
  xKey="weekOf"
  series={[{ key: "free", label: "Free" }, { key: "pro", label: "Pro" }]}
  title="Sign-ups by plan"
  formatValue={(v) => `${v} sign-ups`}
  loading={isFetching}
  error={error?.message}
  onRetry={refetch}
  onPointClick={(row) => openWeek(row.weekOf)}
/>
